key_insight: Learning the subgrid-scale and wall closures jointly inside a differentiable LES solver yields better turbulence predictions than training either closure separately.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to more accurate and transferable wall-modeled LES for turbulent boundary layers across new Reynolds numbers, grids, and domains.
method: Builds a differentiable hybrid neural–CFD solver for WMLES
Uses two composed closures: a trainable neural net plus a fixed physics-preserving layer for SGS and wall modeling
Back-propagates low-order-statistics losses through the coupled flow solver for end-to-end joint optimization
evidence_signal: Validated on a zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layer with posteriori tests over Re_theta = 600–6500, multiple meshes and domains, where it outperformed WMLES baselines and retained accuracy even beyond the training Reynolds-number range.
watch_item: Performance depends on reliable differentiable solver implementation and the coupled training setup; learning closures in isolation was shown to be insufficient.
paper_title: Differentiable Hybrid Neural-CFD Modelling of Wall-Bounded Turbulence: Coupled Learning of Subgrid-Scale and Wall Closures
